design.question: Is the module's purpose obvious from the customer-facing isometric view without relying on its label?
Can the primary equipment, drawer, lid, hose, or work surface be reached and deployed without an obvious obstruction?
Does the visible arrangement support the order in which a user performs the module's core task?
Are stored items divided, restrained, and visually organized for rough-road transport?
Are controls, ports, displays, latches, and service points visible and understandable?
Does the concept visibly communicate a secure stowed state as well as its deployed state?
Are spill, dirt, ventilation, and drainage paths addressed where the module's use requires them?
Are handles, reaches, work heights, and frequently used interfaces plausible for field use?
Does the module read as part of the silver-extrusion, dark-panel ten-module family while retaining a distinct function?
Does the concept include the strongest visible usability cues found in the cited comparable products without copying proprietary styling?

manufacturing.question: Is the structure limited to the released 1-inch 10-Series extrusion family and fixed 18/22-inch cut list?
Can unique cut lengths and custom part count be reduced without losing function?
Are frame joints represented by one compatible bracket-and-fastener architecture rather than mixed systems?
Can skins, trays, dividers, and worktops be made from flat routed or cut sheet with accessible fasteners?
Can drawer slides and latches use the approved shared OTS families and fit within the clear envelope?
Can a technician reach every recurring fastener, latch, slide, pump, connector, and restraint with ordinary tools?
Can the module be assembled, skinned, wired or plumbed, inspected, and serviced in a practical sequence?
Are service, lid, slide, hose, wiring, gasket, and purchased-product clearances explicitly protected?
Does every purchased item refer only to a sourced catalog ID, with sold-out and engineering-hold items clearly identified?
Can incoming parts, assembly completion, motion, leaks, ventilation, and retention be checked with defined evidence?

combined.question: Do manufacturing choices preserve or improve the visible function rather than making the module anonymous?
Are both deployed usability and transport-secure stowage coherent with the selected hardware?
Is the sourced primary product represented with realistic access, restraint, ventilation, and service space?
Can high-wear OTS components be removed and replaced without destroying the frame or custom panels?
Are the heaviest stored products kept low and positively restrained, with unresolved dynamic loads still gated?
Do panel, gasket, drainage, ventilation, and hardware choices match likely dust, water, vibration, and temperature exposure?
Are heat, propane, potable water, grey water, and electrical functions visibly segregated and appropriately labeled?
Does any manufacturing simplification create a new reach, pinch, snag, cleaning, or access problem?
Are shared frame, panel, slide, latch, handle, gasket, and restraint choices maximized across all ten modules?
Is the concept visually complete, separately exportable, source-traceable, and honestly held short of fabrication release where engineering evidence is missing?
